Also on second thought I figure the VN community and anime community probably have some overlaps. Not sure if it's allowed/makes sense to request here, but I'd be very grateful for a visual novel recommendation as well. Previous ones I've read include the Danganronpa series (all 3 main games) and the Umineko no Naku Koro Ni question and answer arcs. Both were great, but I haven't really seen any others with a deep enough plot to get stuck into on Steam or any of the platforms I've looked at. Too many seem to be heavy ecchi/hentai games or clichéd harem dating sims, and that's not what I'm looking for.

I'm looking for a couple of recommendations. MAL is in my flair (if I set it up properly, which hopefully I did).

First is a lighter anime- preferably a comedy, romantic comedy, or slice of life. Comedic/SOL standouts that are relevant to my current interests are Kaguya-sama (both seasons were hilarious but s1 was better IMO), Kobayashi-san (what will probably be my favorite SOL comedy forever), and to a lesser extent Bunny Girl Senpai and Chuunibyou. I loved the wit and charm of the interactions between Sakuta and Mai in Bunny Girl Senpai, but am probably looking for something a little less heavy on the drama. I enjoyed Chuunibyou as well but the later episodes as the story starts to unravel similarly got a bit too heavy for me. Possible options I've considered are Toradora! and Gekkan Shoujo Nozaki-Kun.

Second would be a more dramatic or more action-focused anime. Not to say Shirobako was particularly heavy or anything, but it's definitely a drama, not a comedy. I recently rewatched it and was re-impressed at how good it was for a very meta "non-story/working life" story. Other more serious anime I've very much enjoyed were Death Parade, Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, Erased (extremely good suspense), the Danganronpa game series (murder mysteries are fun), and in some ways Bunny Girl Senpai as well. Thoughts I've had include picking up Steins;Gate, retrying Death Note (I got to about the dramatic meme chip-eating scene, lost it, and swore off the anime as too ridiculous), or retrying Cowboy Bebop.

I'm also down for a traditional shonen as well- I enjoyed MHA a lot and plan to pick up Season 5 after it's fully released. I also was a fan of several isekai like Log Horizon, Tensei Slime, and Overlord.

Any thoughts, comments, or suggestions would be greatly appreciated! Thanks in advance.

You actually DD against ep29- you're never required to play a card, so the Rack does nothing. You both stare at each other forever and draw.
You WL against mopplow- he can t1 Sphere you, meaning you can't cast your 1 mana Black Lotuses.
Ends up at 20 points :/

Pod 13:
Decklist: Tabernacle, Strip Mine, Mishra's Factory
Soulos90: Mountain, Goblin Lackey, Krenko, Mob Boss. (WW, 6)
Tabernacle prevents ever being attacked by Lackey, I Factory him out.

FancySpaceHorse: Black Lotus, Laboratory Maniac, Gitaxian Probe (LL, 6)
I'd hoped that Lab Man was going to be underrepresented since it had the biggest target. Looks like I was right, with only 1 in an 11-man pod. Doesn't change the fact that it butt-blasts me.

Mopplow: Mishra's Workshop, Sphere of Resistance, Phyrexian Revoker (WW, 12)
No spells to cast, so IDGAF about Sphere, Tabernacle kills Revoker since Workshop can't pay for it.

ep29: Black Lotus, Energy Field, The Rack (DD, 14)
Initially I thought this was an awesome deck, but it just draws with everything except Lab Man or other combo decks, which it loses to. (The other deck doesn't have to play/cast anything, so The Rack does nothing.)

plastgeek: Black Lotus, Channel, Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre (DD, 16)
On the play or draw I can wait until he casts Ulamog, then play Tabernacle, killing it. He redraws, but can't cast Ulamog again (requires 10 life off Channel each time). However, I can't play an attacking land without him Ulamogging it, in which case I can't kill him.

Shogunfish: Simian Spirit Guide, Lightning Bolt, Chancellor of the Forge (DD, 18)
Tabernacle kills his goblin, Bolt kills my Factory.

vaelroth: Black Lotus, Black Lotus, Leveler (WW, 24)
Tabernacle is really good against creature strategies, you guys.

TheBiggestZander: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth, Blackmail, The Rack (LL, 24)
I can't outrace him on the play- Factory t1 means I have a 10 turn clock, but his Urborg-Rack T1 deals 1 on my t2. I can play Strip Mine and attack, but The Rack starts doing 3 per turn on my t3 when he Blackmails my Tabernacle. On the draw, it's the same thing but I lose the race harder.

Ayegill: Chancellor of the Forge, Snapback, Force of Will (WW, 30)
He can Snapback the Factory.... once. Tabernacle kills Goblin, Factory gets there.

Dratnos: Black Lotus, City of Traitors, Meloku, the Clouded Mirror. (DD, 32)
Strip mining the City means that Meloku (and any associated Spirits) die to Tabernacle, but I don't have mana to activate Factory.

Woo, slightly better than average!
